entities.summary:
Paramount Pictures is the oldest surviving Hollywood studio and one of the 'Big Five' majors, founded in 1912-1916 and known for producing the first major American feature film, The Squaw Man (1914). Paramount has produced some of cinema's most iconic films: The Birth of a Nation distribution deal, The Ten Commandments (1956), Breakfast at Tiffany's (1961), The Godfather (1972), Chinatown (1974), Saturday Night Fever (1977), Raiders of the Lost Ark (1981), Top Gun (1986), Forrest Gump (1994), Titanic (co-financed, 1997), and Transformers.

Adolph Zukor, who founded Paramount as 'Famous Players Film Company' in 1912, introduced the concept of 'famous players in famous plays' — using stage stars to give film legitimacy, a radical idea. Paramount's invention of the studio system, block booking (forcing theaters to take whole packages of films), and vertical integration (owning theaters) defined Hollywood's oligopoly until the 1948 Paramount Decree forced studios to divest theater ownership.

Paramount's acquisition by Gulf+Western (later Viacom) in 1966 began the era of conglomerate ownership of Hollywood studios. Francis Ford Coppola's The Godfather (1972, Paramount) is frequently cited as the greatest American film and launched the New Hollywood era. The current Paramount Pictures is owned by Paramount Global (formerly ViacomCBS), which in 2024 merged discussions with Skydance Media for control of the company.
